newsitem.title: INDIA: Sluggish consumer demand caps Bombay sugar rally.
newsitem.headline: Sluggish consumer demand caps Bombay sugar rally.

text.p: Bombay sugar prices on Thursday suffered a setback at improved levels with sluggish consumer demand capping a rally, dealers said.
Trading volumes were however low as major players kept away anticipating a government announcement of the free sale quota for next month.
In the ready delivery sugar S-30 slid by five rupees at 1,455/1,475 rupees per quintal while M-30 moved down by 5/10 rupees at 1,470/1,505 rupees per quintal.
"The free sale quota for the current month is 800,000 tonnes and marketmen were expecting the government to announce a quota of 725,000/750,000 tonnes for July," one broker said.
"Even some traders are predicting quota of 800,000 tonnes for July.".
Sugar mill delivery held steady in a limited activity at the mill level. In the mill delivery sugar S-30 was quiet at 1,390/1,410 rupees per quintal so did M-30 at 1,415/1,435 rupees per quintal.
